commands.author: Alix-007

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): time out stalled CONNECT upstreams
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The debug proxy's HTTP `CONNECT` path opened its upstream TCP socket without a deadline. A blackholed or stalled target could therefore leave the client request and capture session pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give upstream CONNECT establishment a 30-second opening deadline. On timeout, the proxy records a local capture error, explicitly destroys the upstream socket, and returns a complete `504 Gateway Timeout` response to the client.

Node's socket timeout only emits an event; it does not close the socket, so explicit destruction is required. Once the upstream emits `connect`, the implementation disables the timer and removes the opening-timeout listener so long-lived CONNECT tunnels do not inherit an idle timeout.

## User Impact

Debug proxy clients now receive a bounded, actionable 504 response when a CONNECT target never establishes. Successfully connected tunnels remain long-lived exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `4862fb81e0aa5821790870e41bfb82682947197c`
- Full CI is green on the exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Node 24.15.0: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts` (5/5 tests passed)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files
- `oxlint` on both changed files
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`
- Node 24.15.0 `net` source was checked directly for pre-connect timeout setup, event-only timeout behavior, timer removal, and destroyed-socket connect handling.
- Independent adversarial review: clean; this is the best fix at the existing CONNECT socket boundary.

### Real debug-proxy behavior

Ran the production `startDebugProxyServer` path from the exact PR head on Linux x64 with Node 24.18.0, outside Vitest. The timeout case used a host-network TCP target whose handshake packets were deliberately dropped; a separate local TCP echo origin exercised an established CONNECT tunnel concurrently. The temporary network rule was removed immediately after the run.

Redacted output:

```text
{"head":"4862fb81e0aa5821790870e41bfb82682947197c","node":"v24.18.0","platform":"linux/x64","path":"production startDebugProxyServer"}
{"case":"blackholed-connect","elapsedMs":30011,"statusLine":"HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout","complete":true}
{"case":"established-tunnel","heldOpenMs":31500,"statusLine":"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established","echoedBeforeDeadline":true,"echoedAfterDeadline":true}
{"case":"capture-record","direction":"local","kind":"error","protocol":"connect","errorText":"CONNECT upstream timed out after 30000ms"}
```

This proves both rank-up paths requested in review: the running debug proxy returns the complete bounded 504 for a real stalled TCP opening, and a successfully established tunnel remains usable after the 30-second opening deadline has elapsed.
